# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** Through the hands of a holy prophet, Wisdom made all their endeavors succeed.

**11:2** They crossed a wasteland where no road had ever been marked, set up camp in regions where no one could travel.

**11:3** They stood their ground against enemies and pushed back every adversary.

**11:4** When they were thirsty, they cried out to you — and you gave them water from bare rock, relief from their thirst out of hard stone.

**11:5** This is the pattern: the very things that punished their enemies became blessings for them in their time of need.

**11:6** When the Nile — the ever-flowing river — was turned to blood as a judgment against those who had decreed the death of children,

**11:7** you gave your people water in abundance, completely unexpectedly,

**11:8** and through the thirst they had suffered, you made clear how severely you had punished their enemies.

**11:9** When they were tested and gently corrected, they came to understand how the ungodly were suffering under judgment and wrath.

**11:10** You dealt with your own people as a father who disciplines with love; you dealt with the others as a strict king handing down a sentence.

**11:11** Whether they were near or far, both groups were equally afflicted.

**11:12** A double grief gripped them — the present pain and the aching memory of what had already passed.

**11:13** When they heard that these people were actually being blessed through the same disasters that were punishing Egypt, they finally recognized the Lord at work.

**11:14** The one they had long ago mocked and abandoned — at the final outcome, they found themselves astonished by him, having thirsted in a way utterly different from how the righteous had thirsted.

**11:15** Because they had followed foolish and unrighteous thinking — the kind that led them astray into worshipping mindless reptiles and worthless crawling things — you sent against them a great swarm of mindless creatures as their punishment,

**11:16** to teach them the principle: you are punished by the very things you sin with.

**11:17** Your all-powerful hand made the world from shapeless matter — it could easily have sent against them whole armies of bears or savage lions,

**11:18** or invented entirely new creatures, terrifying and unknown, breathing fire, roaring smoke, or shooting blazing sparks from their eyes —

**11:19** creatures that could have destroyed the Egyptians not just by the damage they caused but simply by their horrifying appearance.

**11:20** Even without any of this, a single breath from you could have knocked them flat — justice in pursuit, your power's wind scattering them to nothing. But you arrange everything by measure, number, and weight.

**11:21** You always have the option of overwhelming strength. Who could ever stand up to the force of your arm?

**11:22** The whole world before you is like a speck of dust tipping a scale — like a drop of dew on the morning ground.

**11:23** But you show mercy to all, because you can do everything, and you look past human sin to leave room for repentance.

**11:24** You love everything you have made — there is nothing in all existence that you despise. If you had hated something, you would never have brought it into being.

**11:25** How could anything go on existing if you did not will it? How could anything be preserved unless you called it forth?

**11:26** You spare everything — because everything belongs to you, O Master who loves every living soul.
